name: File Type Detector
description: Drop any file and read its real type from the magic bytes — not the extension — and spot mismatches like a .jpg that is actually a PNG.
body:
🔍

Drop any file here or click to browse

Files are read locally — nothing is uploaded

Drop a file to see its real type, magic bytes and extension check.
howto: Drop one or more files onto the dropzone, or click to browse.
The tool reads the first bytes of each file (the magic number) to identify the real format.
Compare the detected type against the file extension.
A mismatch warning means the file was renamed or converted incorrectly — fix it with the right tool before uploading anywhere.
Re-check each file after converting it to confirm the new extension matches.
features: Magic-byte detection for 25+ common formats (images, documents, archives, audio, video, executables)
Extension vs. actual format mismatch detection
Hex preview of the file signature
100% client-side — your files never leave your device

faq.a: Magic bytes are the first few bytes of a file that identify its true format — for example PNG files start with 89 50 4E 47 and PDFs with 25 50 44 46. They reveal the real type no matter what the filename says.

faq.q: Why would a file extension not match its real type?
faq.a: Files get renamed by mistake, downloaded with the wrong extension, or converted without updating the name. This tool catches those cases before you submit or publish them.

faq.q: Can I convert a file with this tool?
faq.a: No — it only detects and validates. Use the Batch File Renamer to fix extensions, the Image Format Converter for images, or a dedicated converter for documents and media.

faq.q: Does this work for every file format in the world?
faq.a: It covers the most common formats plus a generic fallback. Rare or proprietary formats may show as unknown — in that case the extension and file size are still displayed for reference.
